claim: Pluripotent stem (PS) cells possess unlimited proliferative potential and the ability to differentiate into all cell types of the body.
source: PS cells possess the unique feature of unlimited proliferative potential and the ability to differentiate into all cell types of the body.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about pluripotent stem cells.

claim: Induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cell technology enables the easy derivation of PS cells from any individual, including patients with genetic diseases.
source: The advent of induced pluripotent stem (iPS) cell technology enables the easy derivation of PS cells from any individual, including patients with genetic diseases (Takahashi et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Takahashi et al., 2007.

claim: PS cell-derivatives are predominantly embryonic in nature.
source: This latter point in particular has been a conundrum in the field since extensive literature suggests that PS cell-derivatives are predominantly embryonic in nature (Abdelalim and Emara, 2015; Aigha and Raynaud, 2016; Chen et al., 2018; Jiwlawat et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Attempts to induce maturation of PS cell-derivatives involve maintaining the cells in culture for long periods of time, generally longer than one month.
source: To date, attempts to induce maturation of PS cell-derivatives involve maintaining the cells in culture for long periods of time, generally longer than one month (Lainé et al., 2018; Paavilainen et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published studies.

claim: Inhibition of TGFβ signaling enhances in vitro PS cell-derived skeletal muscle maturation.
source: A recent study comparing the transcriptional profile of transgene-free PS cell-derived myotubes with fetal myotubes revealed inhibition of TGFβ signaling as an approach to enhance in vitro PS cell-derived skeletal muscle maturation (Hicks et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Hicks et al., 2018.

claim: Inhibition of the TGFβ signaling pathway through the use of small molecules results in enhanced myotube differentiation and hypertrophy.
source: Notably, inhibition of the TGFβ signaling pathway through the use of small molecules has been extensively reported to result in enhanced myotube differentiation and hypertrophy (Furutani et al., 2011; Liu et al., 2001; Schabort et al., 2009; Watt et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published studies.

claim: A small molecule screening identified four candidates whose combinatorial treatment enhances the maturation of PS cell-derived myotubes in a time frame of 5 days of myotube differentiation.
source: In this study, we performed a small molecule screening and identified four candidates whose combinatorial treatment enhances the maturation of PS cell-derived myotubes in a time frame of 5 days of myotube differentiation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The combinatorial small molecule treatment resulted in a striking increase in the expression profile of neonatal myosin heavy chain (MyHC) isoform.
source: This was evident by the striking increase in the expression profile of neonatal myosin heavy chain (MyHC) isoform as well as in other genes associated with neonatal and adult muscle, as revealed by chromatin accessibility and RNA sequencing analyses.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from chromatin accessibility and RNA sequencing analyses presented in the manuscript.

claim: The combinatorial small molecule treatment improves contractile force generation of three-dimensional (3D) PS cell-derived muscle constructs.
source: Moreover, we demonstrate the usefulness of the combinatory small molecule treatment for inducing maturation and improving contractile force generation of three-dimensional (3D) PS cell-derived muscle constructs, thus contributing to the use of organoid-like platforms for in vitro modeling.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on contractile force measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: Treatment of differentiating PS cells with CHIR99021 for two days results in the expression of early mesoderm marker T and paraxial mesoderm markers MSGN1 and TBX6.
source: This treatment resulted in the expression of the early mesoderm marker T as well as the paraxial mesoderm markers MSGN1 and TBX6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Treatment with LDN193189 and SB431542 from day 4 to day 6 resulted in increased expression of MEOX1, TCF15, PAX3 and FOXC2 on day 6.
source: Treatment of differentiating PS cells from day 4 to day 6 with LDN193189 and SB431542 (+LS) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) resulted in increased expression of MEOX1, TCF15, PAX3 and FOXC2 on day 6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PS cell-derived myotubes remained immature, as indicated by their thin morphology and predominant expression of the embryonic isoform of myosin heavy chain (MYH3).
source: Despite the promising results described above, PS cell-derived myotubes remained immature, as indicated by their thin morphology (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) and predominant expression of the embryonic isoform of myosin heavy chain (MYH3) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological observations and gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: Five compounds (SB431542, DAPT, Dexamethasone, PD0325901, and Forskolin) consistently showed statistically significant increase (p<0.001) in MyHC/DAPI area ratio in myotubes derived from multiple PS cell lines.
source: For the purposes of this study, we selected five compounds that consistently showed statistically significant increase (p<0.001) in MyHC/DAPI area ratio in myotubes derived from multiple PS cell lines (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: S/Da/De/P/F or S/Da/De/P combinatorial conditions showed significant increase in MyHC/DAPI area ratio (>2 fold relative to DMSO).
source: Significant increase in MyHC/DAPI area ratio (>2 fold relative to DMSO) was observed in all combinations (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: S/Da/De/P/F treatment resulted in remarkable increases in fusion index and number of nuclei per myotube.
source: Consistently, this correlated with remarkable increases in fusion index and number of nuclei per myotube in the S/Da/De/P/F condition, which again were unaffected when excluding P but not the other compounds (Figure 1E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-F.

claim: S/Da/De/F (excluding P) consistently resulted in significantly increased expression of all MYH isoforms analyzed, with a more dramatic upregulation observed for neonatal MYH8.
source: Although S/Da/De/P/F or S/Da/De/P combinatorial conditions showed significant increase for some MYH isoforms, our data demonstrated that only S/Da/De/F (excluding P) consistently resulted in significantly increased expression of all MYH isoforms analyzed, with a more dramatic upregulation observed for neonatal MYH8 (neo-MyHC) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Neo-MyHC protein expression was detected only upon S/Da/De/F treatment.
source: Western blot and immunostaining analysis confirmed expression of neo-MyHC at the protein level only upon S/Da/De/F treatment (Figure 2C–D), whereas MYH1 and MYH2 were not detected upon treatment (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot and immunostaining data shown in Figure 2C-D.

claim: Neo-MyHC protein expression only occurs at later stages of human muscle development.
source: Of relevance, a previous study reported that neo-MyHC protein expression only occurs at later stages of human muscle development, thus further confirming the enhanced maturation status of myotubes treated with S/Da/De/F (Cho, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cho, 1993.

claim: S/Da/De/F treatment resulted in thicker and larger myotubes compared to DMSO treatment.
source: As shown by Titin immunofluorescence staining (Figure 2E), both DMSO- and S/Da/De/F-treated myotubes are striated. However, S/Da/De/F treatment resulted in thicker and larger myotubes (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: At day 5 of differentiation, there was dramatic reduction in cell proliferation and increase in differentiation in the S/Da/De/F group compared to DMSO.
source: Interestingly, whereas no differences were observed between DMSO and S/Da/De/F at days 1 and 3 for both parameters, at day 5, we observed dramatic reduction in cell proliferation and increase in differentiation in the S/Da/De/F group (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C-D.

claim: S/Da/De/F treatment induced differential expression of CEBPD and FKBP5 (Dexamethasone targets), HES1 and NOTCH2 (DAPT targets), COL1A1 and ID3 (SB431542 targets), and PPARGC1A (Forskolin target).
source: As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D, we found significant differential expression of CEBPD and FKBP5 (De targets; Luedi et al., 2017; MacDougald et al., 1994; Pan et al., 2010; Pereira et al., 2014; Reddy et al., 2012; Scharf et al., 2011), HES1 and NOTCH2 (Da targets; Huang et al., 2011; Jarriault et al., 1995; Mao et al., 2018), COL1A1 and ID3 (S targets; Lehmann et al., 2018; Ramachandran et al., 2018; Sato et al., 2015) and PPARGC1A (F target; Charos et al., 2012; Martin et al., 2009; Sayasith et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-D and citations to published literature.

claim: S/Da/De/F treatment induced the maturation of PS cell-derived myotubes generated under transgene-free conditions.
source: Of note, S/Da/De/F treatment also induced the maturation of PS cell-derived myotubes generated under transgene-free conditions (Xi et al., 2017) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A-B and a citation to Xi et al., 2017.

claim: S/Da/De/F treatment enhanced differentiation and maturation of MD patient-specific iPS cell-derived myotubes.
source: Consistently, our data showed enhanced differentiation (Figure 3A) and maturation (Figure 3B) of MD patient-specific iPS cell-derived myotubes upon S/Da/De/F treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-B.

claim: S/Da/De/F-treated myotubes were richer in mitochondria than DMSO-treated myotubes.
source: S/Da/De/F-treated myotubes were clearly richer in mitochondria than their DMSO counterparts.
evidence: This claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy observations described in the text and shown in Figure 4.

claim: SR-TT junctions were readily detectable in all S/Da/De/F-treated myotubes, while they remained scarce in the DMSO-treated myotubes.
source: Indeed, these structures were readily detectable in all S/Da/De/F- treated myotubes (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D), while they remained scarce in the DMSO-treated myotubes (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A larger number of S/Da/De/F-treated cells were engaged in fusion (>5 cells) as compared with mainly 2 (or rarely 3) in the DMSO control.
source: Indeed, a larger number of S/Da/De/F-treated cells were engaged in fusion (>5 cells) as compared with mainly 2 (or rarely 3) in the control.
evidence: This claim is supported by ultrastructural examination data described in the text and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: 62,748 and 80,334 chromatin accessible peaks were detected in DMSO- and S/Da/De/F-treated cells, respectively.
source: Following a 2 day treatment, we detected 62,748 and 80,334 chromatin accessible peaks in DMSO- and S/Da/De/F-treated cells, respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Differential analysis of chromatin accessibility identified 2782 peaks displaying increased chromatin accessibility in the S/Da/De/F-treated group.
source: Differential analysis of chromatin accessibility followed by exclusion of loci overlapping to centromeric and other repetitive elements (referred as blacklist; ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012) identified 2782 peaks displaying increased chromatin accessibility in the S/Da/De/F-treated group (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data analysis shown in Figure 5B and a citation to ENCODE Project Consortium, 2012.

claim: Increased chromatin accessibility was detected at genomic elements associated with myogenic genes such as MYOG, MYH3 and the muscle microRNAs MIR206 and MIR133B.
source: As expected, this group included genomic elements associated with myogenic genes such as MYOG, MYH3 and the muscle microRNAs MIR206 and MIR133B (Chen et al., 2006; Kim et al., 2006; Koutsoulidou et al., 2011; Swiderski et al., 2016) (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B, and citations to published literature.

claim: Increased chromatin accessibility was detected at the CEBPD locus, a Dexamethasone target gene in human cells.
source: Similarly, increased chromatin accessibility was detected at the CEBPD locus (Figure 5C), a Dexamethasone target gene in human cells (MacDougald et al., 1994; Pan et al., 2010; Reddy et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5C and citations to published literature.

claim: Significant reduction in chromatin accessibility was observed at loci encoding or regulating downstream target genes of the TGFβ (ID3) and NOTCH (HES1) signaling pathways.
source: In agreement with the biological function of SB431542 and DAPT, we also observed significant reduction in chromatin accessibility at loci encoding or regulating downstream target genes of the TGFβ (ID3) (Ramachandran et al., 2018) and NOTCH (HES1) (Jarriault et al., 1995) signaling pathways. (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and citations to published literature.

claim: S/Da/De/F-specific regions showed enrichment for several motifs associated with known myogenic transcription factors, including MYOG, MEF2, and POU.
source: This analysis showed enrichment for several motifs associated with known myogenic transcription factors, including MYOG, MEF2, and POU (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by motif analysis of ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claim: About 1859 significantly differentially expressed genes were identified, from which about half were downregulated and the other half were upregulated in the S/Da/De/F-treated group compared to controls.
source: We identified about 1859 significantly differentially expressed genes, from which about half were downregulated and the other half were upregulated in the treated group compared to controls (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Ingenuity pathway analysis corroborated the four small molecules (and their targets) as upstream regulators of the differentially expressed genes.
source: To dissect the transcriptome profile associated with S/Da/De/F treatment, we first performed ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA) and corroborated the four small molecules (and their targets) as upstream regulators of the differentially expressed genes, which was evidenced by the 'activation Z-scores' (<-2 or >2) and validated by the overlap p-values (<0.01) (Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by IPA analysis of RNA sequencing data.

claim: The analysis revealed transcription factors and miRNAs involved in muscle differentiation as upstream regulators of changes in gene expression upon S/Da/De/F treatment, including TEAD4, MYF6, KLF4, MEF2A, MEF2C, MIR-133B, MIR-206 and MIR-503.
source: Interestingly, the analysis also revealed transcription factors and miRNAs involved in muscle differentiation as upstream regulators of changes in gene expression upon S/Da/De/F treatment, including TEAD4 (Joshi et al., 2017), MYF6 (Kassar-Duchossoy et al., 2004; Montarras et al., 1991), KLF4 (Sunadome et al., 2011), MEF2A, MEF2C (Liu et al., 2014), MIR-133B, MIR-206 and MIR-503 (Chen et al., 2006; Kim et al., 2006; Koutsoulidou et al., 2011; Sarkar et al., 2010) (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by IPA analysis shown in Figure 6B and citations to published literature.

claim: Skeletal and muscular system development was found the most upregulated physiological system according to IPA data.
source: According to our IPA data, skeletal and muscular system development was found the most upregulated physiological system (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by IPA analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Among upregulated canonical pathways, the analysis identified oxidative phosphorylation and calcium signaling, indicating an increase in mitochondrial biogenesis and muscle contraction, respectively.
source: In addition, among upregulated canonical pathways, the analysis identified oxidative phosphorylation and calcium signaling, indicating an increase in mitochondrial biogenesis and muscle contraction, respectively (Figure 6D), corroborating the increased number of mitochondria observed by TEM (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by IPA analysis shown in Figure 6D and TEM data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Sarcolipin (SLN), a gene reported to play a critical role in mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism in skeletal muscle, was found among the highest expressed genes (around 30-fold) in the treated group.
source: Moreover, Sarcolipin (SLN), a gene reported to play a critical role in mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative metabolism in skeletal muscle (Maurya et al., 2018), was found among the highest expressed genes (around 30-fold) in the treated group (a result we have validated by qPCR; Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and qPCR validation shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A, and a citation to Maurya et al., 2018.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of upregulated genes for biological processes and cellular components identified various muscle function groups, indicating increased muscle differentiation and function.
source: Gene ontology analysis of upregulated genes for biological processes and cellular components identified various muscle function groups, indicating increased muscle differentiation and function (Figure 6E–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 6E-F.

claim: Upregulation of genes such as ENO3, MYF6, CKM, TNNT3, MYH8, ATP2A1, ITGA7 and PRKCQ was found, all reported to be upregulated in fetal, postnatal and adult myotubes in comparison to embryonic myotubes.
source: Consistently, we found upregulation of genes, such as ENO3, MYF6, CKM, TNNT3, MYH8, ATP2A1, ITGA7 and PRKCQ, all reported to be upregulated in fetal, postnatal and adult myotubes in comparison to embryonic myotubes (Biressi et al., 2007a; Burkin and Kaufman, 1999; Hinterberger et al., 1991; Ju et al., 2013; Schiaffino et al., 2015), supporting our observations on the enhancing effect of the combinatorial treatment on myotubes maturation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA sequencing data and citations to published literature.

claim: S/Da/De/F-treated myotubes showed downregulation of MEOX1, PAX3, CDH11, EYA2 and FST, genes known to be expressed at higher levels in embryonic myotubes than in fetal myotubes.
source: Correspondingly, we found that S/Da/De/F-treated myotubes showed downregulation of MEOX1, PAX3, CDH11, EYA2 and FST, genes known to be expressed at higher levels in embryonic myotubes than in fetal myotubes (Biressi et al., 2007b) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and a citation to Biressi et al., 2007b.

claim: 42% of the loci with increased chromatin accessibility upon S/Da/De/F treatment were associated to differentially expressed genes (1727/4145 annotated genes).
source: Upon annotation of the ATAC-seq peaks to the two nearest genes followed by comparison with the transcriptomic data, we observed that 42% of the loci were associated to differentially expressed genes (1727/4145 annotated genes).
evidence: This claim is supported by integrated analysis of ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Loci characterized by increased chromatin accessibility and increased expression are associated with muscle contraction, regulation of calcium storage and muscle development.
source: Gene ontology classification of these two lists of genes confirmed that loci characterized by increased chromatin accessibility and increased expression are associated with muscle contraction, regulation of calcium storage and muscle development (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: There was a remarkable increase in both twitch and tetanus force generation (about 15-fold) in the S/Da/De/F-treated 3D constructs compared to DMSO controls.
source: We found a remarkable increase in both twitch and tetanus force generation in the treated group (about 15-fold; Figure 7A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by contractile force measurement data shown in Figure 7A-B.

claim: Treated-3D constructs expressed higher levels of various MYH isoforms.
source: Gene expression analysis showed that treated-3D constructs expressed higher levels of various MYH isoforms (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Significant increase in expression of MYH1 and MYH2 was observed upon treatment in 3D cultures.
source: Whereas we could not reliably detect upregulation of MYH1 and MYH2 gene expression levels in 2D cultures, we observed significant increase in expression of both genes upon treatment in 3D cultures (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Neo-MyHC was upregulated at the protein level in 3D muscle constructs upon treatment.
source: Neo-MyHC was also upregulated at the protein level as revealed by western blot and immunostaining of the 3D muscle constructs (Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), confirming superior differentiation and maturation.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot and immunostaining data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: In Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), absence of dystrophin at the sarcolemma is compensated to some extent by utrophin during early gestational stages.
source: For instance, in Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), absence of dystrophin at the sarcolemma is compensated to some extent by utrophin during early gestational stages (Helliwell et al., 1992; Pons et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Upon birth, utrophin is located preferentially at the neuromuscular junction.
source: However, upon birth utrophin is located preferentially at the neuromuscular junction (Ohlendieck et al., 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In regenerating fibers, utrophin can be detected at the sarcolemma but is insufficient to sustain its stability, leading to the severe DMD phenotype in the adult muscle.
source: Although in regenerating fibers utrophin can be detected at the sarcolemma (Gramolini et al., 1999), it is insufficient to sustain its stability, leading to the severe DMD phenotype in the adult muscle.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature and inference about disease progression.

claim: SB431542 (TGFβ signaling inhibitor) and DAPT (Notch signaling inhibitor) have been described to promote hypertrophy and fusion of myoblasts lines, respectively.
source: Interestingly, SB431542 (TGFβ signaling inhibitor) and DAPT (Notch signaling inhibitor) have been described to promote hypertrophy and fusion of myoblasts lines, respectively (Kitzmann et al., 2006; Watt et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Dexamethasone has a well-known function in promoting atrophy in myotubes.
source: Dexamethasone was an unexpected finding based on its well-known function in promoting atrophy in myotubes (Hong and Forsberg, 1995; Thompson et al., 1999; Wang et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Forskolin has been reported to increase myoblast proliferation through activation of adenylate cyclase and subsequent phosphorylation and activation of cAMP response element binding protein (CREB).
source: Forskolin has been reported to increase myoblast proliferation through activation of adenylate cyclase and subsequent phosphorylation and activation of cAMP response element binding protein (CREB) (Stewart et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: MEK1 activation during the first 24 hr after switching to terminal differentiation conditions decreases differentiation while at a mid-stage stabilizes MyoD and promotes differentiation.
source: For instance, MEK1 activation during the first 24 hr after switching to terminal differentiation conditions decreases differentiation while at a mid-stage stabilizes MyoD and promotes differentiation (Jo et al., 2011; Jo et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The molecular signature of embryonic and adult myogenesis is not identical.
source: Our findings corroborate the idea that although there are common factors involved in embryonic and adult myogenesis, the molecular signature of these processes is not identical (Czerwinska et al., 2016; Lepper et al., 2009; Wang and Conboy, 2010), and therefore, compounds should not be expected to cause the same effects.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and inference from the study's findings.

claim: The combinatorial treatment is beneficial from the beginning upon switching to terminal differentiation conditions.
source: Interestingly, we found that S/Da/De/F combination dramatically increased fusion, differentiation and maturation of resulting myotubes compared to individual treatments, and this coincided with increased chromatin accessibility in elements associated with myogenic specification at day 2, which suggests that treatment is beneficial from the beginning upon switching to terminal differentiation conditions.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the chromatin accessibility data at day 2.

claim: The combinatorial treatment is beneficial to sustain myotube maturation.
source: Moreover, RNA-seq analysis at day 5 revealed an increase in the expression of genes associated with muscle functionality and maturation processes. This is relevant as it shows that the combinatorial treatment is also beneficial to sustain myotube maturation.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the RNA-seq data at day 5.

claim: The differentiation and maturation switch occur within 5 days upon switching to differentiation medium.
source: Importantly, the differentiation and maturation switch occur within 5 days upon switching to differentiation medium and is applicable to MD patient-specific iPS cell-derived myotubes, in addition to unaffected cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing changes within 5 days of treatment.

claim: The maturation induced by S/Da/De/F treatment is relevant to iPS cell-derived myotubes generated using a transgene-free differentiation protocol.
source: We also found that the maturation induced by this treatment is relevant to iPS cell-derived myotubes generated using a transgene-free differentiation protocol, confirming its broad applicability.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on transgene-free myotubes.

claim: S/Da/De/F treatment enhances the contractile capacity of PS cell-derived 3D muscle constructs.
source: Our data show that S/Da/De/F treatment is not only significant for the expression of genes associated with maturation in 2D cultures, but it also enhances the contractile capacity of PS cell-derived 3D muscle constructs.
evidence: This claim is supported by contractile force measurement data on 3D constructs.

claim: The combinatorial treatment of S/Da/De/F contributes to enhanced myotube differentiation and maturation of PS cell myogenic derivatives.
source: Taken together, we show that the combinatorial treatment of S/Da/De/F contributes to enhanced myotube differentiation and maturation of PS cell myogenic derivatives, and therefore represents an advance for studying skeletal muscle function and disease in vitro.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Each MYH isoform is found predominantly expressed at specific developmental stages: MYH3 for embryonic, MYH8 for neonatal, and MYH1, MYH2 and MYH7 for adult muscle.
source: Expression of MYH isoforms can be used as a readout for the maturation state of generated myotubes, as each MYH isoform is found predominantly expressed at specific developmental stages: MYH3 for embryonic, MYH8 for neonatal, and MYH1, MYH2 and MYH7 for adult muscle (Schiaffino et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: An increase in the ratio of MyHC (+) to DAPI (+) area would indicate thicker myotubes as a consequence of increased multinucleation, hypertrophy and/or enhanced differentiation, which could be potentially accompanied by increased maturation.
source: We reasoned that an increase in the ratio of MyHC (+) to DAPI (+) area would indicate thicker myotubes as a consequence of increased multinucleation, hypertrophy and/or enhanced differentiation, which could be potentially accompanied by increased maturation (Biressi et al., 2007b).
evidence: This is a reasoning statement supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Concentrations ranging from 5 to 20 μM of the selected compounds did not significantly change the MyHC/DAPI area ratio.
source: Since concentrations ranging from 5 to 20 μM of the selected compounds did not significantly change the MyHC/DAPI area ratio (Figure 1—figure supplement 3C), in subsequent studies we used 10 μM for each compound.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Exclusion of S, Da, De or F led to the generation of thinner myotubes compared with the full combinatorial condition, while exclusion of P did not affect myotube morphology.
source: Exclusion of S, Da, De or F led to the generation of thinner myotubes compared with the full combinatorial condition, while exclusion of P did not affect myotube morphology (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological observations shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Neo-MyHC protein expression co-localizes with F-actin in a cross-striation staining pattern, suggesting protein functionality.
source: Furthermore, immunostaining revealed cross-striation staining pattern of neo-MyHC co-localizing with that of F-actin (stained with Phalloidin), suggesting protein functionality (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and inference about functionality.

claim: Both DMSO- and S/Da/De/F-treated myotubes are striated.
source: As shown by Titin immunofluorescence staining (Figure 2E), both DMSO- and S/Da/De/F-treated myotubes are striated.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The small molecule treatment may be particularly relevant at the late stage of differentiation.
source: These data suggest that the small molecule treatment may be particularly relevant at the late stage of differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal analysis of proliferation and differentiation parameters.

claim: Myofibrils reached various degrees of sarcomeric organization even within the same cell in both DMSO and S/Da/De/F conditions.
source: Analysis of a large number of samples at high magnification showed that myofibrils reached various degrees of sarcomeric organization even within the same cell in both conditions (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 4.

claim: The various degrees of sarcomeric organization may be explained by ongoing fusion between cells with different maturation levels or stages.
source: This may be explained by ongoing fusion between cells with different maturation levels or stages (see below).
evidence: This is an inference to explain the observed heterogeneity in sarcomeric organization.

claim: SR-TT junctions produce voltage-dependent intracellular Ca2+ transients upon membrane depolarization and support excitation-contraction coupling.
source: Similar junctions were shown to produce voltage-dependent intracellular Ca2+ transients upon membrane depolarization, and hence, support excitation-contraction coupling (Skoglund et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The high occurrence of SR-TT junctions in treated cells may contribute to the increase in their contraction capacity.
source: Therefore, the high occurrence of SR-TT junctions in treated cells may contribute to the increase in their contraction capacity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed increase in SR-TT junctions and known function of these structures.

claim: Ultrastructural examination revealed ongoing plasma membrane fusion in both DMSO and S/Da/De/F conditions, but the process was more prolific in S/Da/De/F-treated cells.
source: Ultrastructural examination of adjacent cells at high magnification revealed ongoing plasma membrane fusion in both conditions. Such a process was, however, undoubtedly more prolific in S/Da/De/F-treated cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by transmission electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: S/Da/De/F treatment alters the epigenetic landscape of differentiating PS cell-derived myogenic progenitors by increasing chromatin accessibility at elements associated with key myogenic genes and pathways.
source: Based on these data, we conclude that S/Da/De/F treatment alters the epigenetic landscape of differentiating PS cell-derived myogenic progenitors by increasing chromatin accessibility at elements associated with key myogenic genes and pathways, potentially underlying the mechanism of small molecule-induced maturation of myotubes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the integrated analysis of ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: The POU transcription factor Pou2f1 (also known as Oct1), through cooperation with SRF and MEF2, regulates transcription of the fast MyHC (MyHC-2b).
source: Among these, the POU transcription factor Pou2f1 (also known as Oct1), through cooperation with SRF and MEF2, regulates transcription of the fast MyHC (MyHC-2b) (Allen et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Pou6f1 (also called Emb) was identified in a complex with MEF2D and p300, whose function is to control Actc1, an actin isoform expressed in developing skeletal muscle and cardiac muscle.
source: Analogously, Pou6f1 (also called Emb) was identified in a complex with MEF2D and p300, whose function is to control Actc1, an actin isoform expressed in developing skeletal muscle and cardiac muscle (Molinari et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Skeletal myogenesis is accompanied by mitochondrial biogenesis.
source: This makes sense as skeletal myogenesis has been documented to be accompanied by mitochondrial biogenesis (Remels et al., 2010; Sin et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Loci with increased chromatin accessibility and decreased expression demonstrated enrichment for non-myogenic developmental pathways.
source: In contrast, loci with increased chromatin accessibility and decreased expression demonstrated enrichment for non-myogenic developmental pathways (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Dexamethasone may have an opposite role during differentiation of embryonic myotubes compared to adult counterparts.
source: This suggests that dexamethasone may have an opposite role during differentiation of embryonic myotubes compared to adult counterparts, although a detailed mechanism remains to be further dissected.
evidence: This is speculation based on the unexpected finding that dexamethasone enhances maturation in the study.

claim: Forskolin treatment enhances the differentiation efficiency of PS cell-derived progenitors into myotubes.
source: In contrast, our studies show that Forskolin treatment enhances the differentiation efficiency of PS cell-derived progenitors into myotubes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: MEK1 inhibition, through PD0325901, enhanced differentiation of PS cell-derived progenitors.
source: We observed that MEK1 inhibition, through PD0325901, enhanced differentiation of PS cell-derived progenitors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: The development of organoid-like structures provides improved structural organization and enhanced tissue functionality, which are critical in the development of reliable platforms for disease modeling and therapy development.
source: This is relevant as the development of organoid-like structures have been shown to provide improved structural organization and, therefore, enhanced tissue functionality, which are critical in the development of reliable platforms for disease modeling and therapy development (Clevers, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Treatment with CHIR99021 for two days improves skeletal myogenic differentiation from PS cells.
source: To induce mesoderm differentiation of PS cells, we utilized CHIR99021 (GSK3β inhibitor) treatment for two days (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), which we and others have previously reported to improve skeletal myogenic differentiation from PS cells (Borchin et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature and the protocol shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: LDN193189 and SB431542 can induce somitic mesoderm-like cells.
source: Considering the recent literature demonstrating the ability of the BMP inhibitor LDN193189 and the TGFβ inhibitor SB431542 to induce somitic mesoderm-like cells (Xi et al., 2017), we investigated whether these inhibitors would enhance myotube generation in the context of PAX7-induced myogenic differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Xi et al., 2017.

claim: Optimal myogenic specification by PAX7 would be achieved if it was induced when cells are at the peak of somite-like state.
source: Induction of PAX7 expression with doxycycline began on day 5, two days earlier than our standard protocol (Darabi et al., 2012), as we reasoned that optimal myogenic specification by PAX7 would be achieved if it was induced when cells are at the peak of somite-like state.
evidence: This is a reasoning statement that guided the experimental design.

claim: MyHC-expressing myotubes were detected only when cultures were subjected to terminal differentiation following withdrawal of doxycycline.
source: Of note, MyHC-expressing myotubes were detected only when cultures were subjected to terminal differentiation following withdrawal of doxycycline.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental protocol.

claim: The modified protocol (+LS) showed significant improvement in the differentiation efficiency of several of the seven PS cell lines investigated when compared to the unmodified protocol (-LS).
source: Our results showed significant improvement in the differentiation efficiency of several of the seven PS cell lines investigated (unaffected and diseased), when compared to the unmodified protocol (-LS) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The improvement in differentiation efficiency was particularly evident in PS cell lines displaying limited in vitro differentiation potential using the unmodified protocol.
source: This result was particularly evident in PS cell lines displaying limited in vitro differentiation potential using the unmodified protocol.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The Tocriscreen stem cell toolbox kit consists of 80 stem cell modulator compounds.
source: To determine whether small molecule compounds may enhance the maturation of PS cell-derived myotubes, we performed a small molecule library screening using the Tocriscreen stem cell toolbox kit (Tocris). This library consists of 80 stem cell modulator compounds.
evidence: This is a description of the screening library used.

claim: Neo-MyHC protein expression was confirmed in additional three PS cell lines subjected to the combinatorial treatment.
source: Importantly, neo-MyHC protein expression was confirmed in additional three PS cell lines subjected to the combinatorial treatment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Increased pan-MyHC and α-actinin were observed by immunostaining of 3D constructs upon treatment.
source: Increased pan-MyHC and α-actinin were observed as well by immunostaining of 3D constructs upon treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
